Restoration Started and Abandoned: This Pontiac Sat for Years in a Shop, Some Work Done
21 photos
Photo: eBay seller elpasoconnection
1979 Trans Ams are the best Trans Ams, and that’s specifically why this specimen is here today. The car is aiming for a restoration that’d bring it back to its original glory days.
This Trans Am was this close to getting this long-overdue restoration, but unfortunately, not all things are going as planned. The owner explains on eBay that the vehicle was brought to a restoration shop, and despite some work already being done, it ended up abandoned.
It has been sitting for many years, with some parts already missing. It’s now trying to convince a stranger online to take it home and continue this abandoned restoration.
1979 marked the Trans Am’s 10th anniversary . Pontiac celebrated this moment with the TATA, an anniversary model that was fitted with every single option in the entire lineup. Buyers could only choose the engine, but otherwise, everybody received the full package. Production was limited to 7,500 units.
However, the regular Trans Am also sold like hotcakes. The GM brand ended the year with over 117K units shipped to buyers in the States, marking the Trans Am’s best year in history.
This specimen is a Pontiac 400-powered specimen with a 4-speed transmission, but it goes without saying that it needs extensive work in every key area before it can even return to the road. No information was offered about the engine, so its condition is unknown, but my recommendation is that you call the seller and ask all these questions before making an offer.
The black on black Trans Am comes without some parts, though several extras are also included and pictured. “I do have the T-tops and the scoop,” the owner explains on eBay. Putting everything back together will take some time, especially because some parts are missing, but this also depends on your goal.
Building a 1979 Trans Am is not as difficult as it sounds, as the WWW has so many projects waiting for a second chance, so finding a donor priced correctly shouldn’t take long. But at the end of the day, it also depends on the price of this project itself, as the costs of restoring a 1979 Trans Am begin with the restoration candidate’s price.
The seller looks realistic, so I expect this Trans Am to find a new home quite fast. They want $9,500 for this Trans Am, which looks just about right, considering some work has already been done and the vehicle looks quite solid. The Make Offer option has also been enabled, so you should reach out to the seller for additional details.
The car landed on the watchlists of 44 people, and considering the listing goes offline in 7 days, you’d better hurry up to get your hands on this Trans Am project.
